answers_by_date.answer: No right to vote in any election
answers_by_date.basis: National law (Constitution of 1994, arts. 37 and 48; Electoral Code, Ley 19.945, art. 1 in its pre-2012 wording) gave the vote only to citizens ('ciudadanos ... nativos, por opción y naturalizados'). No national provision gave lawfully present foreigners the vote. Local voting by foreigners existed only in provincial law, e.g. Buenos Aires Province Constitution art. 191. The City of Buenos Aires' Ley 334 was not yet in force: it was published 21/02/2000. There is no national-level practice to rate.

answers_by_date.answer: No right to vote in any election
answers_by_date.basis: Same constitutional and Electoral Code rules. Ley 25.871 (B.O. 21/1/2004) art. 11 only commits the State to 'facilitate', 'in accordance with national and provincial legislation', foreigners' consultation or participation in local public life. It creates no right to vote. Provincial and City of Buenos Aires (Ley 334, 2000) local voting for permanent residents is subnational, so the national answer stays 'No'.

answers_by_date.answer: No right to vote in any election
answers_by_date.basis: No change. Decreto 616/2010 (May 2010) postdates this date and does not touch voting. The Electoral Code art. 1 still limited electors to native, by-option and naturalized citizens.

answers_by_date.answer: No right to vote in any election
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 26.774 (B.O. 02/11/2012) replaced Electoral Code art. 1 to lower the voting age: 'Son electores los argentinos nativos y por opción, desde los dieciséis (16) años..., y los argentinos naturalizados, desde los dieciocho (18)'. It kept citizenship as the condition, so foreigners still had no national vote. Local voting stayed a provincial and City matter.

answers.repealed_search: I checked the original 1972 text of the Electoral Code art. 1 and its 2012 replacement (Ley 26.774), Ley 346 art. 7, Ley 25.871 (original text art. 11) and the text of Ley 22.439 on argentina.gob.ar, looking for any national provision granting foreigners the vote. None existed between 2000 and 2020. Every version of the Electoral Code limits electors to citizens. The only foreign-voter rules are subnational: Buenos Aires Province Constitution art. 191 and CABA Ley 334 (2000), the latter repealed and replaced by Ley 6031 from 1/1/2020, which is a replacement, not a narrowing of national law.

answers.starting_answer_concern: Under the MRD's national-law approach the 'No' holds, since no federal norm lets foreigners vote. A reviewer should note, though, that subnational law gave permanent residents local votes throughout 2000-2020: Buenos Aires Province Constitution art. 191 and CABA Ley 334 from February 2000, among others. On the indicator's wording ('local or regional elections') this could support 'Right to vote in local or regional elections' if provincial law were counted. Also, the MRD's citation to Constitution art. 37 is inaccurate: art. 37 guarantees political rights and universal suffrage; it does not confer electoral autonomy on the provinces (that rests on arts. 5, 121-123).
answers.notes: No court ruling relied on. I did not count ICRMW (ratified by Ley 26.202, 2007), because its art. 42(3) leaves political rights to the State's discretion. Implementation is 'Does Not Apply' on all dates. The provincial and City norms are recorded as context only, and I read the Buenos Aires Province constitution from an unofficial copy (PDBA Georgetown).

answers_by_date.answer: No right to run for public office in any election
answers_by_date.basis: The Constitution requires citizenship for national elective office: art. 48 for deputies ('cuatro años de ciudadanía en ejercicio'), art. 55 for senators ('seis años ciudadano de la Nación') and art. 87 for the President ('un ciudadano'). No national norm let foreigners stand for election. Foreigners could be elected municipal councillors only under provincial law, e.g. Buenos Aires Province Constitution art. 191 (five years' residence, special register, at most one third of the council). There is no national-level practice to rate.

answers_by_date.answer: No right to run for public office in any election
answers_by_date.basis: No change. Ley 25.871 (2004) art. 11 is only a commitment to facilitate participation in local public life. It gives no right to stand for office. The constitutional citizenship requirements are unchanged.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'No' holds at national level. Note that the MRD cites Buenos Aires Province Constitution 'Art. 191.3'. In the text read, the foreign-councillor eligibility rule sits in the third base of art. 191 ('si son extranjeros, tengan además cinco años de residencia y estén inscriptos en el registro especial'), and the one-third cap in the sixth. If subnational law were counted, it would support 'Right to run for public office in local or regional elections' throughout 2000-2020.
